options.text: Turn off the stove and cover the pan with a metal lid to smother the flames.

options.text: Turn off the stove and use a fire blanket if you have one.
options.label: safe

options.text: Pour water on the pan to extinguish it.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Blow hard on the flames to put them out.

transcript.text: Okay! I covered it and turned off the stove. The flames stopped but there is smoke.

options.text: Open all windows to let the smoke out.

options.text: Pour water everywhere to cool the stove.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Pouring water near a grease fire risks spreading the grease or causing an electrical short circuit.

options.text: You don't need to evacuate, just stay inside.

options.text: Move everyone upwind, cover mouths with wet cloth, do not touch anything.

options.explanation: This keeps everyone safe.

options.text: Pour sand over the mixture.

options.text: Flood the spill with water.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Use a fan to blow the gas away.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A fan's electrical motor can spark and ignite flammable chemical fumes, causing an explosion.

options.text: Drag the chemical buckets outside.

transcript.speaker: Caller

options.text: Throw sand on the wire.

options.text: Gather bystanders under a nearby roof.

options.text: Use a garden hose to wet down the grass.

transcript.speaker: Caller

options.explanation: Medication can interfere with the body's natural cooling and kidney function during dehydration.

options.text: Leave him alone to sleep it off.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: He needs to be monitored to ensure he doesn't slip into a heat stroke.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! An e-bike battery just exploded in the garage at {location}! There's a chemical fire and the rider's legs are badly burned!

options.text: Do not put water on the battery! Evacuate everyone and drag the rider to a safe distance if possible.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Lithium-ion battery fires react violently to small amounts of water. Evacuation is key.

options.text: Get the burned rider outside immediately. Do not breathe the toxic battery smoke.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Lithium-ion fires release highly toxic gases. Moving to safety is the priority.

options.text: Throw buckets of water on the exploding battery.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water can worsen a lithium battery fire and spread the chemicals.

options.text: Try to unplug the e-bike from the wall.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Approaching an exploding battery risks severe burns and electrocution.

options.text: Use a blanket to smother the e-bike.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Lithium battery fires generate their own oxygen and will easily burn through a blanket.

options.text: Leave the rider inside and run away.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You must assist the injured person to safety if you can do so safely.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We are outside! The rider is crying in pain from the burns. The garage is full of thick white smoke.

options.text: BFP and MDRRMO are on the way. Cool the rider's burns with cool, clean running water if available outside.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Cooling burns with cool (not ice) water helps stop tissue damage.

options.text: Do not apply ice to the burns. Keep everyone far away from the toxic smoke.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Ice causes further tissue damage to burns. Staying away from smoke is vital.

options.text: Put butter or toothpaste on the burns.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Greases and home remedies trap heat in the burn and cause infections.

options.text: Open the garage door wider to let the smoke out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening the door gives the chemical fire more oxygen, accelerating it.

options.text: Try to peel the burnt clothing off the rider's legs.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Peeling burnt clothing can rip off the skin. Medics must do this in a controlled way.

options.text: Put ice packs directly on the burned skin.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Ice causes frostbite on damaged skin and worsens the burn injury.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! My cat knocked over a lit candle and the curtains caught fire at {location}!

options.text: Get everyone out of the room immediately and close the door behind you.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Closing the door contains the fire and buys you time to evacuate safely.

options.text: Do not try to pull down the burning curtains. Evacuate now.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Pulling burning fabric will cause it to fall on you, causing severe burns.

options.text: Throw a glass of water on the curtains.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A small amount of water won't stop a curtain fire, and you will get too close to the flames.

options.text: Try to stomp on the burning fabric.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Stomping on tall, burning curtains is ineffective and highly dangerous.

options.text: Open the window to let the smoke out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening the window provides fresh oxygen and creates a draft, spreading the fire rapidly.

options.text: Use a blanket to beat the flames.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Beating a vertical fire with a blanket can spread burning embers around the room.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We are out of the room and the door is closed. Everyone is safe.

options.text: Evacuate the house entirely and wait outside for BFP.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Safest action to ensure nobody is trapped if the fire spreads.

options.text: Do not go back inside for your pets, let firefighters know when they arrive.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Firefighters have the gear to rescue pets. Going back in is lethal.

options.text: Go back in to quickly check if the fire died down.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening the door will feed the fire oxygen and expose you to a backdraft.

options.text: Hide in the bathroom and turn on the shower.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Bathrooms offer no protection against toxic smoke, which will seep under the door.

options.text: Start packing your clothes into suitcases.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never delay evacuation to save property. Your life is the priority.

options.text: Go to the kitchen to get a fire extinguisher.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: If the fire is already spreading up the curtains, it is too late for a small extinguisher.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! The wind blew our campfire into the dry bushes at {location} and it's spreading fast!

options.text: Move everyone away from the smoke and back to the main road or clearing.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Getting out of the path of a brush fire is the top priority.

options.text: Do not try to outrun the fire uphill. Move downhill to a safe zone.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Fire travels faster uphill. Moving downhill or to a clearing is safer.

options.text: Use your drinking water bottles to put it out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Small bottles of water cannot stop a spreading brush fire.

options.text: Try to beat the bushes with a large stick.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Beating dry bushes can fan the flames and spread burning embers onto yourself.

options.text: Run uphill away from the fire.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Fires move incredibly fast uphill due to heat rising. You cannot outrun it.

options.text: Climb a tree to stay safe.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Climbing a tree traps you as the fire burns the tree and the smoke rises.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We ran to the main road. The smoke is very thick now.

options.text: Stay on the paved road and flag down the BFP trucks.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Paved roads act as firebreaks and provide a safe zone to wait.

options.text: Cover your mouths with clothing to filter some of the smoke.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Helps reduce smoke inhalation while waiting in the safe zone.

options.text: Go back to save your camping tents.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Tents are highly flammable and not worth risking your life.

options.text: Walk through the smoke to find a better view.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Thick smoke causes disorientation and suffocation very quickly.

options.text: Drive your car through the burning bushes.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Cars can stall in thick smoke, trapping you in a burning vehicle.

options.text: Hide in your tent and zip it up.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A tent provides no protection from heat or smoke.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! I put a food wrapper with metal foil in the microwave at {location} and it sparked and caught fire!

options.text: Keep the microwave door closed and unplug it if you can do so safely.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Keeping the door closed starves the fire of oxygen, and unplugging cuts the power.

options.text: Do not open the microwave door. The fire needs oxygen to grow.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A contained appliance fire will usually burn itself out if deprived of oxygen.

options.text: Open the door and pull the burning wrapper out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening the door feeds the fire oxygen, and pulling it out will burn your hands.

options.text: Throw a glass of water inside the microwave.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water on a live electrical appliance can cause a lethal electric shock.

options.text: Press the start button to run the fan.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Running the microwave further powers the electrical fire.

options.text: Try to blow the fire out through the vents.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Blowing into the vents pushes oxygen in and forces toxic smoke back at you.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I kept it closed and unplugged it. The fire seems to have stopped, but it's smoking a lot.

options.text: Do not open it yet. Wait for BFP to arrive and inspect it.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The materials are still superheated and could reignite if exposed to air.

options.text: Evacuate the kitchen to avoid breathing the toxic smoke.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Burning plastics and metals release dangerous fumes.

options.text: Open it quickly to check if it's really out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening it prematurely can cause a sudden flare-up.

options.text: Plug it back in to test if it works.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The internal wiring is damaged and will likely cause another immediate fire.

options.text: Spray air freshener into the vents to hide the smell.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Air fresheners are highly flammable and can ignite from the residual heat.

options.text: Throw the whole microwave into the trash bin.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving a hot, smoking appliance can cause a fire in the trash.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: PNP! There is a ticking backpack left alone under a bench at the bus stop at {location}!

options.text: Tell everyone to clear the area and move at least 100 meters away immediately.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Standard protocol for a suspicious package is immediate evacuation of the blast radius.

options.text: Do not use your cell phone near the bag. Walk far away before continuing this call.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Radio waves from cell phones can sometimes trigger electronic detonators.

options.text: Open the bag carefully to see if there's an ID.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never touch or open a suspicious package. Moving it can trigger an explosive.

options.text: Pick it up and carry it to a trash bin.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Carrying an explosive device is extremely lethal.

options.text: Kick the bag lightly to see what's inside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Any impact can detonate a sensitive explosive device.

options.text: Take a selfie with the bag to post online.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Staying near the bag puts your life in imminent danger.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I told everyone to run. We are very far away now.

options.text: Stay behind solid cover like a concrete wall if possible. PNP bomb squad is responding.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Solid cover protects against shrapnel if an explosion occurs.

options.text: Do not let anyone walk back towards the bus stop.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Perimeter control is essential until police secure the area.

options.text: Go back and retrieve your own bags from the bench.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Property can be replaced. Risking your life for a bag is not worth it.

options.text: Hide behind a glass bus shelter.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Glass shatters during explosions and becomes deadly flying shrapnel.

options.text: Try to throw rocks at the bag to see if it stops ticking.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Impact can trigger a detonation.

options.text: Tell people it's just a prank and they can go back.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You cannot know if it's a prank. Treat all threats seriously.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: PNP! A man I met playing online games is parked outside my house at {location} and says he's waiting for me to come out!

options.text: Ensure all doors and windows are locked. Do not go outside.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Physical barriers protect you from predators. Never meet strangers from the internet.

options.text: Do not engage with him or reply to his messages. Stay hidden. PNP is on the way.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Ignoring the predator denies them control while police arrive to intercept him.

options.text: Go outside with a baseball bat to confront him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Highly dangerous. He could easily disarm you or have a weapon of his own.

options.text: Tell your parents you are going for a quick walk to meet him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never meet online strangers in person. Tell your parents the truth immediately.

options.text: Open the front door slightly to talk to him through the screen.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: He can easily kick open a screen door and force his way inside.

options.text: Invite him in so your parents can meet him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Inviting a potential predator into your home endangers your entire family.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I locked the doors and told my parents. He is honking his horn now.

options.text: Stay away from the windows. Officers will be there in minutes.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Staying out of sight keeps you safe and prevents the situation from escalating.

options.text: Keep your phone close and do not delete his messages, they are evidence.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Digital evidence is crucial for PNP to build a case against cyber predators.

options.text: Yell out the window for him to go away.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Engaging him verbally might provoke him to break a window.

options.text: Take photos of him using flash from the window.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The flash will reveal your location and might cause him to act aggressively.

options.text: Tell him you are calling the police.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Warning him might cause him to flee before police arrive to arrest him.

options.text: Sneak out the back door to run to a neighbor's house.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: He might see you leaving. You are safest inside a locked house.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: PNP! Some teenagers are spray-painting the walls and breaking windows at the school at {location}!

options.text: Stay out of sight. Note their descriptions and what they are wearing.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Being a good witness from a safe distance is the best way to help police.

options.text: Do not confront them. They are currently committing a crime and might be violent.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Vandals can turn aggressive if confronted by civilians.

options.text: Run up and yell at them to stop.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Confronting criminals often leads to physical assault.

options.text: Throw rocks at them from a distance.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Throwing objects escalates the situation to mutual violence.

options.text: Walk over and try to take a selfie with them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This puts you directly in danger and might provoke an attack.

options.text: Perform a citizen's arrest on the spot.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Citizen arrests are dangerous and can lead to severe injury or legal trouble.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: They are walking towards the back gate. I can see their faces clearly.

options.text: Give me their descriptions. PNP officers are pulling up quietly.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Providing real-time updates helps officers intercept the suspects safely.

options.text: If they leave in a vehicle, try to get the license plate number without being seen.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: License plates are the fastest way to track fleeing suspects.

options.text: Chase them down the street so you don't lose them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Chasing suspects puts your life in danger.

options.text: Yell 'The police are coming!' to scare them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Warning them allows them to escape before officers arrive.

options.text: Go inspect the broken windows immediately.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You might get cut by glass or contaminate the crime scene.

options.text: Try to block their escape path with your body.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: They will physically harm you to escape.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: PNP! Two high school boys are fighting at the park near {location} and one has a heavy metal pipe!

options.text: Move to a safe distance and do not try to break up the fight yourself.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Intervening in an armed fight is extremely dangerous for a civilian.

options.text: Keep other kids away from the area. PNP is responding quickly.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Crowd control prevents others from getting injured by stray swings.

options.text: Jump in the middle and try to grab the pipe.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will very likely be struck by the pipe and seriously injured.

options.text: Try to trip the boy with the pipe from behind.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Engaging in the fight makes you a target for assault.

options.text: Yell insults at the attacker to distract him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Distracting an angry armed person will redirect their violence toward you.

options.text: Throw a rock at the person with the pipe.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This escalates the violence and makes you a participant in the assault.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: The boy with the pipe hit the other guy! The victim is on the ground bleeding!

options.text: PNP and an ambulance are arriving now. Stay back until police disarm him.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Wait for professionals to secure the scene before providing first aid.

options.text: Do not approach the victim until the attacker has fled or is arrested.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Approaching while the attacker is armed puts you at risk of being the next victim.

options.text: Run up to the victim and start doing CPR.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: CPR is for heart failure, not bleeding, and the attacker is still present.

options.text: Tackle the attacker while his back is turned.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You are risking your life against an armed and violent suspect.

options.text: Grab the pipe while he's not looking.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Trying to disarm him can lead to a fatal struggle.

options.text: Tell the victim to stand up and fight back.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Encouraging a severely injured person to fight worsens their injuries.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: MDRRMO! My little sister is choking on a hard candy at {location}! She can't cough or breathe!

options.text: Perform the Heimlich maneuver (abdominal thrusts) immediately!
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The Heimlich maneuver creates pressure that forces the object out of the airway.

options.text: Stand behind her, make a fist above her belly button, and pull inward and upward fast.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Correct technique for abdominal thrusts.

options.text: Stick your fingers down her throat to grab it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A blind finger sweep often pushes the object deeper into the airway.

options.text: Give her a glass of water to wash it down.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water will not clear a completely blocked airway and will go into the lungs.

options.text: Tell her to jump up and down.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Jumping is completely ineffective and wastes precious seconds.

options.text: Have her lie on her back and wait for the ambulance.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: She will suffocate before the ambulance arrives. You must act immediately.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I did it! The candy popped out! She is crying and coughing now.

options.text: Encourage her to keep coughing to clear her throat completely.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Coughing is the body's natural and safest way to clear the airway.

options.text: MDRRMO is still coming to check her throat for any damage.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Medical evaluation is necessary after choking and abdominal thrusts.

options.text: Give her a piece of bread to soothe her throat.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Her throat is irritated; giving solid food right away is a choking hazard.

options.text: Slap her hard on the back while she is sitting up.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Back blows are for partial blockages when the person is bent forward. Doing it upright can cause injury.

options.text: Cancel the ambulance, she is fine now.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Thrusts can cause internal bruising, and her throat needs a checkup.

options.text: Tell her to hold her breath to calm down.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: She needs to take deep breaths to recover oxygen.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: MDRRMO! I got stung by a bee at {location}. My throat feels tight and my voice is raspy!

options.text: Sit down and try to stay calm. Do you have an EpiPen or allergy medication nearby?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A tight throat indicates a severe allergic reaction. An EpiPen is needed immediately.

options.text: Do not exert yourself. Keep your airway clear while MDRRMO arrives.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Resting prevents the heart from pumping the allergen through the body faster.

options.text: Try to suck the venom out of the sting.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Does not work for bee stings and delays critical medical treatment.

options.text: Run back home as fast as you can to get medicine.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Running circulates the venom faster and worsens the reaction.

options.text: Drink a hot cup of tea to soothe your throat.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Your throat is swelling shut. Drinking fluids poses a massive choking risk.

options.text: Squeeze the stinger with tweezers to pull it out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Squeezing the stinger injects more venom into your skin. Scrape it off instead.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I don't have an EpiPen! Breathing is getting harder.

options.text: Unlock your front door if you are inside, then sit down near the entrance.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Ensures paramedics can enter immediately without breaking the door if you pass out.

options.text: Stay on the line with me. Do not try to walk or drive anywhere.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Driving while experiencing anaphylaxis is lethal.

options.text: Try to stick your fingers down your throat to clear the swelling.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This will trigger the gag reflex, cause vomiting, and completely block your airway.

options.text: Go to the bathroom and splash water on your face.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: If you pass out in the bathroom, it will be harder for paramedics to find and treat you.

options.text: Eat an antihistamine pill quickly.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Pills take too long to work for anaphylaxis and are a severe choking hazard right now.

options.text: Lay flat on your back and raise your legs.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Lying flat makes it significantly harder to breathe when your airway is swelling.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! A car just crashed into a fire hydrant and a light pole at {location}! There's water spraying everywhere and the driver is stuck!

options.text: Keep away from the water! The downed light pole might have electrified the puddle!
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Water conducts electricity perfectly. Stepping into the puddle could cause instant electrocution.

options.text: Do not approach the car. Wait for emergency services to secure the power lines.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Approaching a vehicle tangled in live wires is deadly for civilians.

options.text: Wade through the water to pull the driver out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: High risk of electrocution from the downed light pole touching the water.

options.text: Try to plug the fire hydrant with your jacket.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Pressurized water from a hydrant can easily break bones or sweep you away.

options.text: Touch the car handle to see if the door opens.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: If the car frame is electrified by the pole, touching it will electrocute you.

options.text: Use a metal crowbar to pry the car door open.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Metal conducts electricity. You will be electrocuted if the car is energized.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I told everyone to stay back. The driver is conscious but trapped inside. He says he feels tingling!

options.text: Tell him to stay completely still inside the car and not touch the metal frame.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The rubber tires insulate the car. If he steps out and touches the ground and car simultaneously, the electricity will pass through him.

options.text: Tell him BFP and power utility are arriving to cut the electricity safely.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Reassuring the victim keeps them from making a panicked, fatal mistake.

options.text: Tell him to jump out of the car as far as he can.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: If he touches the car and the ground at the same time, he will be electrocuted.

options.text: Throw him a rope to pull him out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A wet rope conducts electricity and will electrocute you both.

options.text: Tell him to push the live wire off the car.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Touching a live wire from inside the car is instantly fatal.

options.text: Run up and smash the window to pull him through.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will step in electrified water and die before reaching the window.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! My neighbor is burning dry leaves in their backyard at {location} and the fire caught our wooden fence!

options.text: Keep your family away from the fence. Tell your neighbor to stop if it is safe to do so.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Safety first. Maintaining distance prevents burns from sudden flare-ups.

options.text: Do not try to hose it down if the fire is too large. Evacuate if it nears your house.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A large fence fire can spread to the house quickly. Evacuation is the priority.

options.text: Jump the fence to throw dirt on it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Jumping a burning fence puts you directly in the fire zone and risks severe burns.

options.text: Try to knock the fence down.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A burning fence is structurally weak and can collapse on top of you.

options.text: Use a bucket of gasoline to burn it out faster.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Gasoline is highly explosive and will cause a massive fireball.

options.text: Ignore it, fences don't burn fast.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Dry wooden fences can act as a wick, spreading fire directly to nearby houses.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: The fence is almost fully burned and it's getting close to my garage!

options.text: Evacuate your house immediately. Move everyone to the front street.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: If the fire is threatening a structure, you must evacuate to a safe zone.

options.text: Do not open the garage door. Wait outside for BFP.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Opening the garage can feed the fire oxygen and draw it inside.

options.text: Run into the garage to move your car.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never risk your life to save property. Garages hold flammable chemicals.

options.text: Spray the roof of the garage with a small hose.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Staying close to a spreading fire exposes you to radiant heat and toxic smoke.

options.text: Go to the backyard and start throwing water on the garage.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You might get trapped in the backyard if the fire surrounds you.

options.text: Hide in the basement until the fire department arrives.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Basements are death traps during a fire as smoke and heat accumulate.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! The lights on our dry Christmas tree at {location} short-circuited and the whole tree is in flames!

options.text: Evacuate the house immediately. A dry tree burns incredibly fast.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A dry Christmas tree can engulf a room in flames in less than 30 seconds.

options.text: Do not try to unplug it now. Just get out and close doors behind you.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Closing doors slows the fire's spread. It is too late to unplug it safely.

options.text: Throw buckets of water on the tree.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This is an electrical fire. Throwing water can cause a lethal electric shock.

options.text: Try to drag the burning tree outside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Dragging a burning tree will spread fire to the carpet and severely burn you.

options.text: Use a blanket to smother the tree.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The fire is too large and intense; the blanket will simply catch fire.

options.text: Run around the tree to unplug all the lights.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Getting close exposes you to extreme heat and toxic smoke from burning plastic ornaments.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We ran outside! The living room window just cracked from the heat!

options.text: Stay far back from the house. BFP is on the way.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Windows breaking can cause sudden backdrafts or flashovers.

options.text: Ensure everyone in your family is accounted for outside.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Accounting for everyone ensures firefighters know if a rescue is needed.

options.text: Go back in to save the Christmas presents.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: No material item is worth risking your life in a fully involved room fire.

options.text: Break the rest of the windows to let the smoke out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Breaking windows gives the fire a massive supply of oxygen, causing it to explode in size.

options.text: Open the front door to throw the garden hose inside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening the door feeds the fire and exposes you to intense radiant heat.

options.text: Go to the backyard to check the back door.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Stay in front so firefighters can find you and get information quickly.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! I left my hair straightener on a towel in the bathroom at {location} and the towel is on fire!

options.text: Unplug the straightener if you can reach the plug safely without touching the fire.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Removing the power source is the safest way to handle a small appliance fire.

options.text: Close the bathroom door to contain the fire and get everyone outside.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Closing the door starves the fire of oxygen and stops smoke from spreading.

options.text: Throw the burning towel into the toilet.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Picking up a burning towel will burn your hands and could drop fire onto the floor.

options.text: Leave the door open to air out the smoke.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Leaving the door open feeds oxygen to the fire and fills the house with toxic smoke.

options.text: Splash water from the sink onto the plugged-in straightener.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water on a plugged-in appliance is a major electrocution hazard.

options.text: Beat the fire with another dry towel.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will likely just catch the second towel on fire.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I closed the door and we are outside, but I can hear aerosol cans popping inside!

options.text: Do not go back inside. Exploding aerosols can blow the door open or cause a rapid fire spread.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Aerosol cans like hairspray are highly explosive when heated.

options.text: Wait for BFP to arrive. They have protective gear for chemical explosions.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Firefighters are trained and equipped to handle explosive hazards.

options.text: Go open the bathroom door slightly to see what exploded.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening the door exposes you to toxic smoke, flames, and flying debris.

options.text: Run to the breaker box to turn off the power.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: If the house is evacuated, re-entering to find the breaker box is too dangerous.

options.text: Try to spray a garden hose through the bathroom window.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Spraying water into a room with a live electrical fire and exploding aerosols is dangerous.

options.text: Go back in to grab your jewelry from the bedroom.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The fire can spread quickly from the bathroom to the rest of the house.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! I was charging my phone under my pillow at {location} and it caught fire! The mattress is burning!

options.text: Get out of the bedroom immediately and close the door behind you.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Closing the door contains the highly toxic smoke from the lithium battery and mattress.

options.text: Do not throw water on the battery fire. Evacuate the house.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Lithium-ion batteries react violently with small amounts of water.

options.text: Try to smother the mattress with another blanket.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Lithium fires generate their own oxygen. Blankets will only fuel the fire.

options.text: Grab the burning phone to throw it out the window.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Touching a lithium battery fire will cause severe, deep chemical burns.

options.text: Pour a glass of water on the mattress.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water on a lithium battery can cause it to explode and spray burning chemicals.

options.text: Try to drag the burning mattress into the hallway.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving a burning mattress spreads the fire and exposes you to lethal toxic gases.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I got out of the room. The smoke is so thick and smells like strong chemicals.

options.text: Evacuate everyone from the house now. Do not breathe that smoke.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Battery fire smoke contains highly toxic chemicals like hydrogen fluoride.

options.text: Go outside and stay there. BFP is responding.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The only safe place is outside, upwind from the smoke.

options.text: Open all the windows in the hallway to air it out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening windows creates a draft that pulls the fire out of the bedroom.

options.text: Hold your breath and run back in for your laptop.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: One breath of toxic chemical smoke can knock you unconscious.

options.text: Hide in the closet until the fire department arrives.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Closets offer no protection from smoke, which is the deadliest part of a fire.

options.text: Try to fight the fire from the doorway with a wet towel.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A wet towel will not stop a lithium battery fire or protect you from the toxic fumes.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! The oven in my kitchen at {location} is on fire! There's thick smoke everywhere!

options.text: Keep the oven door closed! Turn off the oven if it is safe to reach the knob.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Keeping the door closed starves the fire of oxygen, usually putting it out safely.

options.text: Evacuate the house. Do not open the oven door.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: If there is too much smoke, evacuating is the safest choice.

options.text: Open the oven door to throw baking soda on it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening the door feeds the fire oxygen and causes a dangerous flare-up into your face.

options.text: Throw a bucket of water into the oven.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water hits hot grease and vaporizes instantly, causing an explosive fireball.

options.text: Try to pull the burning food out with oven mitts.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving burning food spills hot grease and spreads the fire to the kitchen floor.

options.text: Leave the oven on so it burns off the grease.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Leaving the heat on will continue to fuel the fire until it escapes the oven.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I turned it off and kept the door closed! The flames stopped, but the kitchen is very smoky.

options.text: Evacuate outside and wait for BFP to clear the smoke safely.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Smoke inhalation is dangerous. Let professionals ventilate the house.

options.text: Do not open the oven to check on it yet. Wait for BFP.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The oven is still extremely hot and opening it could cause the grease to reignite.

options.text: Open the oven door just a little bit to let the smoke out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Even a little oxygen can cause a flash fire from the superheated grease inside.

options.text: Turn on the stove fan and stay inside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Stove fans can draw heat and flames up into the grease-filled exhaust ducts, starting a wall fire.

options.text: Try to quickly wipe down the stovetop while you wait.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You are staying in a toxic, smoky environment unnecessarily.

options.text: Turn the oven back on to a lower temperature to finish cooking.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This will immediately restart the grease fire.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: PNP! A man in a white van at {location} keeps driving slowly next to me and asking me to get in!

options.text: Run in the opposite direction the car is facing and go to a safe public place.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Cars cannot easily drive backwards. Running the opposite way creates immediate distance.

options.text: Yell for help loudly to attract attention and do not approach his car.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Drawing attention deters kidnappers. Staying away from the vehicle is critical.

options.text: Go up to his window to tell him no.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Approaching the vehicle puts you within grabbing distance.

options.text: Walk normally and ignore him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Ignoring him does not create distance. You need to actively seek safety.

options.text: Throw a rock at his car to scare him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Provoking a predator can escalate the situation and make him aggressive.

options.text: Try to secretly take a photo while standing next to him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Focus on escaping first. Lingering to take a photo gives him time to grab you.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I ran the other way into a convenience store. He drove away quickly!

options.text: Stay inside the store with the employees. PNP is on the way to you.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A well-lit public place with other adults is the safest place to wait for police.

options.text: Try to remember his face and the license plate number if you saw it.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: This information is vital for the police investigation.

options.text: Leave the store to walk the rest of the way home.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: He might be circling the block waiting for you to leave the safe zone.

options.text: Go back outside to see if he comes back.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Leaving a safe area puts you back in danger.

options.text: Borrow a bike to chase after his van.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never chase a potential kidnapper. Let the police handle the pursuit.

options.text: Tell the cashier it was just a joke.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Stranger danger is never a joke. You must report it so others stay safe.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: PNP! I'm a cashier at {location} and someone just stuffed expensive items in their bag and is walking to the door!

options.text: Do not physically block the door. Get a good description of the suspect.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Confronting a shoplifter can escalate into a violent robbery or assault.

options.text: Note what they took and which direction they go when they leave.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Providing a direction of travel helps PNP intercept them safely outside.

options.text: Tackle them before they exit.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Physical confrontation is dangerous; the suspect might be armed.

options.text: Lock the doors so they can't leave.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Trapping a criminal inside with innocent people can cause a hostage situation or violent panic.

options.text: Yell at them that they are under arrest.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Yelling can provoke a violent reaction. Let them leave and observe safely.

options.text: Throw a display rack at them to slow them down.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Throwing objects is assault and puts everyone in the store at risk.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: They left the store and ran towards the subway station. I locked the door after them.

options.text: Good. Stay inside and preserve any CCTV footage for the officers arriving.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: CCTV is the best evidence for prosecuting theft.

options.text: Do not touch the shelves they took items from; officers may check for prints.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Preserving the crime scene aids the investigation.

options.text: Run out after them to see which train they get on.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Following a criminal is dangerous and leaves your store vulnerable.

options.text: Tell all the customers to leave the store immediately.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Customers might be witnesses. Ask them to stay to give a brief statement.

options.text: Start cleaning up the area where the theft happened.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Cleaning up destroys potential evidence like fingerprints or dropped items.

options.text: Close the store for the rest of the day.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Not necessary; just secure the specific area until police arrive.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: MDRRMO! My friend is having a severe asthma attack at the gym at {location}. She doesn't have her inhaler!

options.text: Have her sit upright and try to keep her calm. Encourage slow, steady breaths.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Sitting upright keeps the chest open. Panic worsens breathing difficulties.

options.text: Loosen any tight clothing around her neck and chest. MDRRMO is on the way.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Removing physical restrictions helps her breathe easier.

options.text: Have her lie flat on her back.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Lying flat makes it much harder for the lungs to expand during an asthma attack.

options.text: Give her a paper bag to breathe into.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This is for hyperventilation, not asthma. It dangerously reduces oxygen levels.

options.text: Tell her to do jumping jacks to clear her lungs.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Physical exertion will worsen an asthma attack and consume the little oxygen she has.

options.text: Give her a large cup of cold water to chug.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Drinking quickly while gasping for air poses a severe choking risk.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: She is sitting up and we loosened her jacket. Her breathing is very wheezy.

options.text: Stay with her and keep reassuring her. The ambulance will be there shortly.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Constant monitoring and emotional support help prevent panic.

options.text: Do not give her any food or drink while she is struggling to breathe.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Prevents choking while the airway is restricted.

options.text: Try to force her to lie down so she rests.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never force an asthmatic person to lie down; let them find the posture that helps them breathe best (usually sitting forward).

options.text: Offer her someone else's inhaler if you can find one.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Sharing prescription medication is dangerous and could cause an adverse reaction.

options.text: Carry her outside to get fresh air.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving her can cause exertion. Keep her still and let paramedics move her with oxygen.

options.text: Tell her to hold her breath for 10 seconds to stop the wheezing.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: She is already deprived of oxygen; holding her breath will make her pass out.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: MDRRMO! A stray dog just bit my leg deeply at {location}. It's bleeding a lot and the dog ran away!

options.text: Apply firm, direct pressure to the bite with a clean cloth to stop the bleeding.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Direct pressure is the standard and safest way to control bleeding.

options.text: Sit down and elevate your leg if possible while applying pressure.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Elevating the wound above the heart helps slow down severe bleeding.

options.text: Try to suck the dog's saliva out of the wound.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Ineffective and introduces human mouth bacteria into an already dirty wound.

options.text: Wrap it very tightly with a tourniquet.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Tourniquets are only for life-threatening arterial bleeds that won't stop with direct pressure.

options.text: Run after the dog to catch it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will increase the bleeding by running and risk getting bitten again.

options.text: Pour bleach on the wound to kill the rabies.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Bleach destroys healthy tissue and worsens the injury. Rabies must be treated medically with vaccines.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I am pressing down hard with a towel. The bleeding is slowing down.

options.text: Keep the pressure on. Paramedics will clean it properly and transport you for a rabies shot.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Professional cleaning and rabies post-exposure prophylaxis are mandatory for stray dog bites.

options.text: Do not remove the towel to check the wound; add another on top if it bleeds through.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Removing the towel disrupts blood clotting and restarts the bleeding.

options.text: Take the towel off to wash it with puddle water.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Dirty water will cause severe infections. Let paramedics clean it with sterile saline.

options.text: Cancel the ambulance, a band-aid is enough now.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A deep stray dog bite carries a high risk of rabies and severe infection. Hospital care is required.

options.text: Try to squeeze the wound to push the blood out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Squeezing damages tissue and worsens bleeding.

options.text: Wrap the towel tightly with duct tape to cut off circulation.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Cutting off circulation can lead to tissue death and amputation. Firm pressure is enough.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! The house next door at {location} is fully on fire! I can hear someone screaming from the second-floor window!

options.text: Stay far away from the house. Tell the person to stay low and seal their door with clothing if they can.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Sealing the door buys them time against the smoke while firefighters arrive.

options.text: Do not run inside. BFP and MDRRMO are arriving in less than two minutes.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Firefighters have breathing apparatus and ladders. A civilian entering a blazing house will die.

options.text: Run into the burning house to save them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will become a second victim. Toxic smoke causes unconsciousness in seconds.

options.text: Tell them to jump from the second story window immediately.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Jumping can cause fatal injuries. Unless flames are burning them, they should wait for firefighter ladders.

options.text: Spray the second-story window with a garden hose.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A small hose is ineffective, and spraying water near the victim can create scalding steam.

options.text: Park your car directly under the window to catch them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Cars are hard surfaces that cause severe injuries if fallen upon, and you are blocking the fire truck's access.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: They are hanging out the window coughing! Thick black smoke is pouring out over their head!

options.text: Tell them to stay low on the windowsill and hold on. The fire trucks are pulling up now!
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Staying low keeps them below the thickest toxic smoke while rescue is imminent.

options.text: Make sure the street is clear for the fire engines and ambulance to park.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Clearing the path ensures the fastest possible rescue deployment.

options.text: Tell them to climb up onto the roof.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Roofs collapse during fires, and heat and smoke rise. It is the most dangerous place to go.

options.text: Run up to the house with a blanket to catch them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A civilian holding a blanket cannot safely catch a falling adult; both will be severely injured.

options.text: Tell them to go back inside and try the stairs.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The stairs act as a chimney for smoke and heat. Going back inside is fatal.

options.text: Try to set up a small household ladder.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Small ladders are unstable and delay professional rescue. You are putting yourself in the collapse zone.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: PNP! I'm at the park at {location} and a man in a black van just grabbed a little boy and pulled him inside! They drove off!

options.text: Which direction did they go? Can you describe the van and the license plate?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: This is the most critical information for PNP to intercept the vehicle immediately.

options.text: Stay where you are to give responding officers a full statement. Do not chase them.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Chasing suspects can lead to dangerous collisions or a hostage situation.

options.text: Get in your car and try to run them off the road.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Civilians ramming cars is deadly, especially when a kidnapped child is inside.

options.text: Run around the park shouting to see if anyone knows the boy.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This delays giving critical directional information to PNP.

options.text: Try to call the boy's parents if you don't know who they are.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You cannot find the parents without losing precious seconds. Talk to the dispatcher.

options.text: Post about it on Facebook before talking to me.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Social media is slower than radio dispatch. PNP needs the information right now.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: They turned North onto the highway! The license plate was ABC-1234. It had tinted windows!

options.text: I am broadcasting this to all PNP units now. Can you describe the man or the boy?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Broadcasting the plate immediately sets up roadblocks. Descriptions help identify them.

options.text: Are there any other witnesses around you? Keep them there.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Multiple witnesses might have seen different crucial details.

options.text: Forget the description, just try to follow them on foot.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You cannot outrun a vehicle on foot, and you must stay at the crime scene.

options.text: Go search the area where the van was parked to look for clues.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Walking over the area can destroy tire tracks or dropped evidence.

options.text: Tell everyone in the park to go home.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Witnesses need to stay to be interviewed by detectives.

options.text: Try to guess why the man took him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Stick to the facts. Speculating wastes time during an active abduction.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: PNP! There are some older teenagers at the school gate at {location} forcing younger students to give them their lunch money!

options.text: Stay out of sight. I am dispatching an officer to intercept them.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Staying safe while police arrive is the best approach to minor extortion.

options.text: Do not confront them yourself. Are any weapons visible?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Knowing if they are armed changes the PNP response from patrol to priority.

options.text: Go up and start a physical fight with the older kids.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Starting a fight can lead to serious injuries and legal trouble.

options.text: Tell the younger kids to fight back.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Encouraging children to engage in violence against older kids is highly dangerous.

options.text: Throw rocks at the bullies from across the street.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Throwing rocks is assault and escalates the situation.

options.text: Yell at them that you are filming them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This might provoke them to attack you to take your phone.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I don't see any weapons. They are just pushing the kids against the fence.

options.text: Keep observing safely. A patrol car will be there in two minutes.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Observing safely ensures you can provide accurate statements.

options.text: Can you describe what the teenagers are wearing?
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Descriptions help police catch them if they run.

options.text: Run over and grab the kids away from them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You might get assaulted in the process.

options.text: Tell the victims to just give them all their money.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You should not advise victims on compliance unless there is a deadly weapon.

options.text: Go to the principal's office to complain.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Leaving the scene means you can't update the police when they arrive.

options.text: Start honking your car horn repeatedly.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This might cause the bullies to panic and harm the kids before fleeing.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! Someone shot a firework and it landed on my neighbor's roof at {location}! The shingles are on fire!

options.text: Go knock on your neighbor's door to evacuate them immediately.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The occupants might not know their roof is burning. Alerting them saves lives.

options.text: Do not climb onto the roof. BFP is on the way with ladders.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Civilian roof falls are common and deadly, especially on a burning structure.

options.text: Grab a ladder and climb up to hose it down.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Slipping or falling through a weakened, burning roof is highly dangerous.

options.text: Throw water balloons at the roof.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water balloons will not put out a structural roof fire.

options.text: Tell the neighbor to climb into the attic to check the ceiling.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The attic will fill with toxic smoke and trap them.

options.text: Shoot more fireworks at it to knock the burning one off.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This will undoubtedly start more fires.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I got them out! We are all standing on the street. The fire is spreading across the roof!

options.text: Stay clear of the house. Make sure no one parks in front of the fire hydrant.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Fire engines need immediate access to hydrants to fight structural fires.

options.text: Keep everyone at a safe distance in case the roof collapses.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Roof collapses can send burning debris flying outwards.

options.text: Have the neighbor go back in to grab their wallet.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never re-enter a burning building. The ceiling could collapse at any second.

options.text: Try to spray the roof from the ground with a garden hose.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A garden hose lacks the pressure to reach a roof effectively and keeps you too close.

options.text: Move your cars right next to the house to protect them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Cars parked near a fire can melt or catch fire from radiant heat.

options.text: Break the first-floor windows so firefighters can get in.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Breaking windows unnecessarily causes drafts that feed the fire.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! I left my iron on in the laundry room at {location} and the board cover caught fire!

options.text: Unplug the iron if you can do so safely, then evacuate the room.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Removing the electrical source prevents the fire from reigniting once extinguished.

options.text: Close the laundry room door to starve the fire of oxygen.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A closed door contains the fire and toxic smoke.

options.text: Pour a bucket of water on the live iron.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Pouring water on plugged-in appliances causes electrocution.

options.text: Try to carry the burning ironing board outside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving a burning object spreads the fire and exposes you to severe burns.

options.text: Beat the fire with dry clothes from the hamper.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Dry clothes are highly flammable and will catch fire.

options.text: Open the laundry room window to let the heat out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening the window provides a rush of oxygen that makes the fire bigger.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I unplugged it and closed the door. The smoke alarm is going off everywhere.

options.text: Evacuate the house and wait outside for BFP.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: If smoke is spreading, the house is unsafe to be in.

options.text: Do not open the laundry room door again.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Opening the door could cause a backdraft or spread smoke.

options.text: Go turn off the main water valve to the house.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Not necessary for a fire, and delays your evacuation.

options.text: Hide in the garage until the alarm stops.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You must evacuate entirely outside to be completely safe.

options.text: Go back to the laundry room to check if the fire died.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never check on a closed fire; it exposes you to sudden flare-ups.

options.text: Turn on all the ceiling fans to blow the smoke away.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Fans spread toxic smoke faster and can feed hidden flames.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! We spilled paint thinner in the garage at {location} and the fumes reached the water heater! It flashed into a fire!

options.text: Get everyone out of the garage and house immediately. Do not breathe the fumes.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Chemical fires spread rapidly and produce extremely toxic smoke.

options.text: Do not open the garage door any wider if you are already outside.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Keeping doors closed limits the oxygen available to the chemical fire.

options.text: Try to cover the spilled thinner with a towel.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The towel will ignite instantly, spreading the fire to your hands.

options.text: Try to turn off the water heater's gas valve.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You must walk near the flames and fumes to reach it, risking severe burns.

options.text: Throw buckets of water on the paint thinner.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water will not extinguish chemical fires and will spread the burning liquid.

options.text: Use a broom to sweep the burning thinner out the door.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Sweeping burning liquid will splash fire onto you and your surroundings.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We are outside. The fire in the garage is growing fast and there are more chemicals in there!

options.text: Move far away from the house. Tell firefighters about the chemicals when they arrive.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Chemicals can cause explosions. Firefighters need this information.

options.text: Keep your neighbors informed to stay back.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Protects neighbors from potential explosions or toxic smoke clouds.

options.text: Run back in to save your car.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Garages with chemical fires can explode. A car is not worth your life.

options.text: Try to spray the garage from the driveway.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Standing in the driveway puts you in the blast zone of exploding chemicals.

options.text: Go to the backyard to look through the window.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Windows can blow out during chemical fires, showering you with glass.

options.text: Open the front door to let the smoke out of the house.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This will pull the garage fire into the main house via drafts.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! The ceiling exhaust fan in our bathroom at {location} is making a loud buzzing noise and shooting sparks!

options.text: Keep everyone out of the bathroom and close the door.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Closing the door contains any fire that might start and blocks falling debris.

options.text: If you know where the main breaker is, flip it off. Otherwise, evacuate.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Cutting power stops the short circuit. Evacuating is safest if you cannot.

options.text: Try to hit the fan with a broom handle.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Hitting a live electrical fixture risks electrocution and drops burning plastic on you.

options.text: Splash water up onto the ceiling fan.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Throwing water on electrical sparks causes severe electrocution.

options.text: Stand underneath it with a bucket to catch the sparks.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You are putting yourself directly in danger of falling fire and melted plastic.

options.text: Turn the fan switch on and off repeatedly to reset it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This will cause more arcing and accelerate the fire.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I flipped the breaker off, but now there is smoke coming from under the bathroom door!

options.text: The fire may have spread into the ceiling. Evacuate the house immediately.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Fires inside the ceiling/attic are extremely dangerous and can collapse the roof.

options.text: Do not open the bathroom door. BFP is arriving soon.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Opening the door provides oxygen to the fire.

options.text: Open the door and try to spray a fire extinguisher at the ceiling.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: If the fire is in the ceiling, a standard extinguisher will not reach it.

options.text: Go into the attic to investigate the smoke.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Attics fill with toxic smoke quickly and you could fall through a burning ceiling.

options.text: Turn the power back on to see if it stopped smoking.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This will reignite the electrical short.

options.text: Ignore it, it's just leftover smoke.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Smoke means there is active combustion. You must evacuate.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! Our charcoal grill was too close to the house at {location} and the vinyl siding is melting and catching fire!

options.text: Move everyone away. Do not try to move the hot grill now.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Moving a burning grill can tip it over, spreading hot coals.

options.text: Evacuate the house. Fire behind siding can spread into the walls quickly.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Siding fires often breach the exterior and enter the wall cavities.

options.text: Try to push the hot grill away with your bare hands.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will suffer severe burns.

options.text: Spray the siding with a garden hose while standing next to the grill.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water hitting hot coals creates scalding steam, burning you.

options.text: Throw a bucket of water on the grease tray.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water on grease causes a fireball.

options.text: Open the front door to see if there is smoke inside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening doors changes the draft and can pull the exterior fire inside.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We are away from the house. The flames are climbing up the wall toward the roof!

options.text: Stay clear of the house. Make sure your neighbors are aware.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The fire can spread to neighboring houses. Alerting them is crucial.

options.text: Wait for BFP to arrive. Do not re-enter the house.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The walls could be filled with toxic smoke.

options.text: Run inside to grab the fire extinguisher from the kitchen.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The house may already be compromised with toxic smoke.

options.text: Climb onto the roof to spray it with a hose.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Climbing near a spreading fire risks deadly falls and severe burns.

options.text: Try to rip the burning siding off with your hands.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Melted vinyl siding sticks to skin and causes deep burns.

options.text: Go to the backyard and try to pull the grill away.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You are putting yourself back into the danger zone.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: MDRRMO! My brother got hit in the face with a basketball at {location} and his nose has been bleeding heavily for 20 minutes!

options.text: Have him sit up straight and pinch the soft part of his nose firmly.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Pinching the soft part applies pressure directly to the bleeding vessels.

options.text: Have him lean slightly forward, not backward, so he doesn't swallow blood.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Swallowing blood causes nausea and vomiting.

options.text: Tell him to tilt his head as far back as possible.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This causes blood to drain down the throat, leading to choking or vomiting.

options.text: Stuff tissues deep into his nostrils.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Removing the tissues later will tear the newly formed clot and restart the bleeding.

options.text: Have him lie flat on his back.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Increases blood pressure in the head and worsens the bleeding.

options.text: Tell him to blow his nose to get the blood out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Blowing the nose dislodges clots and makes the bleeding worse.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: He is leaning forward and pinching. He says he feels a little dizzy.

options.text: Keep him seated and keep the pressure on for at least 10 straight minutes.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: It takes time for blood to clot. Releasing pressure too early restarts it.

options.text: MDRRMO is arriving. Do not let him stand up if he feels dizzy.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Dizziness from blood loss can cause fainting and a dangerous fall.

options.text: Let go of his nose to check if it stopped.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Checking interrupts the clotting process.

options.text: Give him a hot cup of coffee to wake him up.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Hot liquids dilate blood vessels and worsen bleeding.

options.text: Tell him to stand up and walk around.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Walking increases heart rate, pushing more blood out.

options.text: Slap his back to help him focus.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Unnecessary physical impact can worsen his condition.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: MDRRMO! A woman just fainted in the crowd at the festival in {location}! She is unresponsive!

options.text: Check if she is breathing normally. If she is, lay her on her back and elevate her legs.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Elevating the legs helps restore blood flow to the brain after fainting (syncope).

options.text: Give her space. Ask the crowd to step back to let fresh air in.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Crowds generate heat and consume oxygen. She needs fresh air to recover.

options.text: Splash cold water directly on her face to wake her up.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Splashing water on an unconscious person can cause them to inhale the water and choke.

options.text: Try to prop her up into a sitting position immediately.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Sitting her up pulls blood away from the brain, prolonging unconsciousness.

options.text: Shake her violently by the shoulders.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Violent shaking can cause neck or spinal injuries.

options.text: Try to force a piece of candy into her mouth.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Putting food in an unconscious person's mouth is a lethal choking hazard.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: She is breathing, and we elevated her legs. She is starting to open her eyes.

options.text: Tell her to stay lying down. Do not let her stand up yet.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Standing too quickly after fainting will likely cause her to faint again.

options.text: Keep the crowd back and wait for the paramedics to evaluate her.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Fainting can be a sign of a serious underlying medical condition.

options.text: Help her stand up so she can walk it off.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: She needs to recover fully before attempting to stand.

options.text: Give her a strong energy drink immediately.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Stimulants are dangerous if her heart rhythm caused the fainting.

options.text: Tell her she is fine and cancel the ambulance.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Only a medical professional should clear her after losing consciousness.

options.text: Try to carry her through the crowd.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Carrying an injured person without a stretcher risks dropping them or worsening their condition.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! Two cars crashed at the intersection of {location}! One driver is hurt and there's gasoline leaking all over the road!

options.text: Keep everyone away from the gasoline. Do not smoke or use flares!
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Gasoline vapors are highly explosive and easily ignited by a spark.

options.text: PNP, BFP, and MDRRMO are responding. Tell everyone to stay on the sidewalk.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A multi-agency response is required to manage traffic, fire risk, and medical needs safely.

options.text: Walk through the gasoline to pull the driver out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Walking in fuel covers your shoes in it, making you a severe fire hazard.

options.text: Try to wash the gasoline away with bottled water.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water floats gasoline and will spread the flammable liquid further down the street.

options.text: Light a flare to warn other cars.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Lighting a flare near a fuel spill guarantees a massive explosion.

options.text: Start directing traffic through the spill.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Cars driving through fuel can ignite it with hot exhaust pipes or sparks.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: The driver is conscious inside the car but says his neck hurts. The smell of gas is very strong.

options.text: Tell the driver to turn off the engine if he can, but do not move his head or neck.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Turning off the engine reduces spark risk. Immobilizing the neck prevents paralysis.

options.text: Stay at a safe distance. Firefighters will secure the spill with foam.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: BFP uses special foam to smother gasoline vapors safely.

options.text: Drag him out of the car by his arms.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Dragging someone with a neck injury can permanently paralyze or kill them.

options.text: Throw a blanket over the gasoline puddle.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The blanket will soak up the fuel and become a massive fire hazard.

options.text: Tell the driver to climb out of the window.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving with a neck injury is dangerous, and jumping into a fuel spill is worse.

options.text: Pour sand over the driver to protect him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Pouring things on victims causes panic and obscures injuries.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! I was using the blender at {location} and the motor started smoking and sparking!

options.text: Unplug it from the wall immediately if it's safe to touch the cord.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Cutting the power is the fastest way to stop an electrical motor fire.

options.text: Do not pour water on the smoking base. Unplug it and move away.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Pouring water on a live appliance risks severe electrocution.

options.text: Pour water into the blender to cool it down.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water conducts electricity and will cause a dangerous shock or explosion.

options.text: Pick it up and carry it to the sink.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving a burning appliance exposes your hands and clothes to the fire.

options.text: Turn the blender speed to low to let it cool off.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Any continued power will worsen the electrical short circuit.

options.text: Throw a dry towel over the sparking motor.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The sparks will quickly ignite the towel, creating a larger fire.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I unplugged it! It stopped sparking but there's a terrible burning plastic smell in the kitchen.

options.text: Leave the blender alone on the counter. Do not touch it.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The internal components are still superheated and could burn you.

options.text: Evacuate the kitchen to avoid breathing the fumes.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Burning plastic releases highly toxic gases.

options.text: Open the blender to see what broke inside.
options.label: unsafe
