options.explanation: Opening it exposes you to toxic smoke and potential burns.

options.text: Plug it back in to a different outlet to test it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The appliance is destroyed and will short circuit again immediately.

options.text: Use an air freshener spray to clear the smell.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Aerosol sprays are highly flammable and can ignite on the hot blender.

options.text: Throw the hot blender into the plastic trash bin.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The residual heat can melt the bin and start a secondary fire.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! My little brother was playing with matches at {location} and set his bedsheets on fire!

options.text: Get your brother out of the room right now and close the door!
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Closing the door isolates the fire and protects the rest of the house from smoke.

options.text: Evacuate the house. Bedsheet fires spread to mattresses in seconds.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Mattresses contain highly flammable polyurethane foam that burns violently.

options.text: Hide your brother in the closet so he doesn't get in trouble.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: He will suffocate from the toxic smoke. Closets offer zero protection.

options.text: Try to pull the sheets off the bed.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The burning sheets will wrap around you, causing severe burns.

options.text: Yell at him to put it out himself.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A child cannot fight a fire and will be quickly overcome by smoke.

options.text: Go to the kitchen to find a glass of water.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: By the time you return, the entire room will be engulfed.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We are out of the room, but my brother wants to go back for his favorite toy!

options.text: Do not let him go back inside! Hold his hand and get outside immediately.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Never re-enter a burning building for property or toys.

options.text: Tell him BFP is on the way to put out the fire.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Reassuring him helps prevent him from running back in a panic.

options.text: Run in quickly to grab the toy for him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You risk your own life to save a replaceable object.

options.text: Let him go quickly if he knows exactly where it is.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Children often hide under beds in a fire and become trapped.

options.text: Open the bedroom door to see if it's safe to grab it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening the door causes a rush of oxygen, creating a lethal fireball.

options.text: Tell him to go through the window from the outside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Breaking windows feeds the fire and puts him back in the danger zone.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! I had too many things plugged into an extension cord at {location} and the rug underneath it is burning!

options.text: Evacuate the room and close the door.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Containing the fire and evacuating is the safest protocol for civilians.

options.text: Go to the main breaker and turn the power off to the house if you know how.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Cutting the main power stops the electrical short safely from a distance.

options.text: Pour a glass of water on the rug.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water on a live extension cord causes electrocution.

options.text: Try to pull the rug out from under the furniture.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Pulling the rug spreads the fire across the room and exposes you to flames.

options.text: Unplug the cords while standing on the burning rug.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will suffer severe burns to your feet and risk electrocution.

options.text: Stomp on the fire with your shoes.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Your shoes and pants can easily catch fire, and you risk a shock.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I closed the door, but smoke is pouring under it really fast!

options.text: Evacuate the entire house right now. The fire is spreading.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Thick smoke means the fire is out of control. Immediate evacuation is required.

options.text: Wait outside for the fire engines. Do not go back inside.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Once out, stay out.

options.text: Roll up a towel and stuff it under the door.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Wastes time and keeps you inside a burning house.

options.text: Open the front and back doors to let the smoke blow through.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening exterior doors creates a wind tunnel that accelerates the fire.

options.text: Go to the kitchen to fill buckets of water.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Buckets of water are useless against a room fire and delay your escape.

options.text: Hide in the basement until they arrive.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Smoke fills the house quickly, making basements a lethal trap.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! I sprayed hairspray near a lit candle at {location} and the spray caught fire! Now the vanity is burning!

options.text: Get out of the bathroom immediately. Aerosol cans can explode if they get hot.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Aerosol cans act like small bombs in a fire. Evacuation is vital.

options.text: Close the door behind you to trap the fire and smoke.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Closing the door isolates the explosive hazard from the rest of the house.

options.text: Try to put it out with a wet towel.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Staying close puts you in the blast radius of exploding cans.

options.text: Throw the burning hairspray can into the toilet.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Picking up a superheated aerosol can will burn you, and it may explode in your hand.

options.text: Spray more hairspray to blow the flames out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Hairspray is highly flammable propellant. You are feeding the fire.

options.text: Turn on the sink and splash water blindly.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water will not stop the aerosol risk and you are staying in the danger zone.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We are outside. I heard a loud pop from the bathroom!

options.text: That was likely the aerosol can exploding. Stay outside and do not re-enter.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Explosions can blow the door open and spread fire instantly.

options.text: Move further away from the house in case the fire spreads to the roof.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Bathroom vents can carry fire straight into the attic.

options.text: Go check if the explosion put the fire out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Explosions scatter burning materials, making the fire much worse.

options.text: Run back in to save your expensive makeup.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: No property is worth risking your life.

options.text: Try to peek through the bathroom window from outside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: If another can explodes, the window will shatter into your face.

options.text: Go turn off the water main.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water is not the issue here; staying far away is the priority.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! The power bank in my backpack at {location} just popped and is shooting out thick white smoke!

options.text: Drop the backpack immediately and move far away. Do not breathe the smoke.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Lithium battery smoke contains toxic gases like hydrogen fluoride.

options.text: Evacuate the area. Lithium battery fires burn extremely hot and fast.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Thermal runaway cannot be easily stopped by civilians.

options.text: Open the backpack to try and take the power bank out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will suffer severe chemical burns and it may explode in your face.

options.text: Try to stomp on the backpack.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Crushing a burning lithium battery causes a violent explosion.

options.text: Pour your water bottle on it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Small amounts of water react violently with lithium and spread the fire.

options.text: Pick the backpack up and throw it outside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The extreme heat will melt through the bag onto your skin.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: It's on the floor smoking, and now flames are shooting out of it!

options.text: Evacuate the room entirely and close the door.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Isolating the fire is the safest action. Let BFP handle the chemical fire.

options.text: Make sure no one tries to go near it. The fumes are deadly.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Preventing others from breathing the smoke saves lives.

options.text: Try to push it out the door with a broom.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The battery can explode, sending shrapnel at you.

options.text: Smother it with a thick winter coat.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Lithium fires generate their own oxygen; the coat will just become more fuel.

options.text: Spray it with an ordinary fire extinguisher.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Standard dry chemical extinguishers do not cool a lithium battery enough to stop thermal runaway.

options.text: Take a deep breath and run past it to escape.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: If there is another exit, use it. Do not go near the toxic smoke.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: PNP! I'm at the busy street corner near {location} and there's a toddler walking around by themselves, crying!

options.text: Stay with the child but do not try to put them in your car. PNP is responding.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Putting a lost child in your car can be legally misinterpreted. Stay in public.

options.text: Try to keep them calm and keep them safely on the sidewalk away from traffic.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The primary danger is the child wandering into the busy road.

options.text: Pick them up and take them to your house to be safe.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Taking a child to a private location is extremely suspicious and dangerous legally.

options.text: Leave them alone but post a photo on Facebook to see if anyone knows them.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You must physically stay with the child to ensure they don't walk into traffic.

options.text: Yell at the people walking by to see who lost their kid.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Yelling can scare the child and make them run.

options.text: Walk them down the street knocking on every door.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Walking away from the spot makes it harder for the panicked parents or police to find you.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I am sitting on a bench with them. A woman just ran up screaming that it's her baby!

options.text: Observe the child's reaction. If the child is happy and calls her 'mom', it is likely safe.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A child's reaction is a strong indicator of a true parental bond.

options.text: Tell the woman police are on the way and ask her to wait just to be sure.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Officers can quickly verify identity to ensure the child's absolute safety.

options.text: Refuse to let the woman near the child until police arrive.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Physically blocking a panicked mother can cause a violent altercation.

options.text: Just walk away immediately without saying anything.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You should confirm the situation with the arriving officers.

options.text: Demand to see the woman's ID yourself.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You do not have the authority to demand ID; let the police handle verification.

options.text: Tell the woman she is a terrible mother.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Accidents happen. Insulting a panicked parent escalates the situation unnecessarily.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: MDRRMO! My teammate collapsed at the outdoor field at {location}! He is confused, his skin is red and completely dry!

options.text: Move him into the shade immediately and fan him to cool him down.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Red, dry skin and confusion mean severe heatstroke. Cooling him is critical.

options.text: Apply cool, wet cloths to his neck, armpits, and groin. Heatstroke is a severe emergency.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: These areas have large blood vessels close to the skin, cooling the core body temperature quickly.

options.text: Force him to drink a gallon of ice water right now.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Forcing a confused person to drink can cause choking or vomiting.

options.text: Cover him with a blanket because he is shivering.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Shivering in heatstroke means his brain's temperature control is failing. A blanket will cook him.

options.text: Have him stand up and walk to the locker room.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Walking increases exertion and core temperature. Carry him or let him rest.

options.text: Give him salt tablets immediately.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Salt tablets without adequate water can worsen cellular dehydration.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We moved him to the shade and put wet towels on him. He just passed out!

options.text: Check if he is breathing normally. If he is, roll him onto his side (recovery position).
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The recovery position keeps the airway clear if he vomits.

options.text: Keep cooling him aggressively. The ambulance is almost there.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Brain damage begins quickly if the core temperature is not lowered.

options.text: Start doing CPR chest compressions.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Do not do CPR if he is still breathing normally.

options.text: Pour a bucket of ice water directly on his face.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This can cause shock or drowning if he inhales the water.

options.text: Try to hold his mouth open to give him air.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Unnecessary and dangerous. Just tilt his head back slightly if he is on his back.

options.text: Slap his face to wake him up.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: He is unconscious from heat injury; slapping him will not wake him and only causes harm.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: MDRRMO! A student in my classroom at {location} just fell to the floor and is shaking violently!

options.text: Clear the area around him of desks and chairs so he doesn't hit his head.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Protecting the person from physical injury during the seizure is the main goal.

options.text: Do not try to hold him down. Place something soft, like a jacket, under his head.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Holding someone down can cause dislocated joints or broken bones.

options.text: Put a spoon or a wallet in his mouth so he doesn't swallow his tongue.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: It is impossible to swallow your tongue. Putting objects in the mouth breaks teeth and causes choking.

options.text: Try to pin his arms and legs to the floor to stop the shaking.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Restraining a seizing person causes severe muscle tears and joint injuries.

options.text: Splash cold water on his face to snap him out of it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You cannot stop a seizure with water. It only poses a choking hazard.

options.text: Start doing CPR immediately.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Seizing people are usually still breathing. CPR is for cardiac arrest.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: The shaking stopped after about two minutes. He is breathing but he won't wake up.

options.text: Roll him gently onto his side. This keeps his airway clear of saliva or vomit.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The postictal state (after a seizure) causes deep unresponsiveness. The recovery position is crucial.

options.text: Stay with him and monitor his breathing until paramedics arrive.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Continuous monitoring ensures you can act if he stops breathing.

options.text: Try to force him to drink some water.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Giving water to an unresponsive person causes them to choke and aspirate.

options.text: Yell his name loudly and shake him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: He is exhausted and recovering neurologically. Let him rest.

options.text: Try to lift him into a chair.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: He cannot support his own weight and could fall again.

options.text: Cover his face with a wet towel to wake him up.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Covering the face restricts breathing, which is dangerous.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! We were having a party at {location} and the second-floor wooden balcony just collapsed! People fell!

options.text: Do not try to move anyone who is severely injured unless there is an immediate fire.

options.text: Keep everyone who is uninjured away from the debris. The structure is unstable.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The remaining structure could collapse further, injuring more people.

options.text: Start digging through the heavy wooden beams yourself.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Try to pull people out by their arms.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Pulling arms can severely worsen spinal, neck, or bone injuries.

options.text: Tell the victims to stand up and walk it off.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Adrenaline masks pain. Walking on broken bones causes severe damage.

options.text: Climb up the broken balcony to see who is still up there.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The structure is compromised and will likely fall under your weight.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I told people to stay back! There are three people on the ground screaming in pain.

options.text: Tell them help is arriving in minutes. Try to keep them still and calm.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Reassurance prevents victims from moving and causing further injury.

options.text: If anyone is bleeding heavily, tell a bystander to apply pressure without moving the victim.

options.explanation: Bleeding control is the only reason to touch a fall victim.

options.text: Try to drag them all into a group so the medics can treat them together.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Dragging victims causes catastrophic spinal injuries.

options.text: Give them alcohol from the party to numb the pain.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Alcohol thins the blood, worsening bleeding, and interferes with medical treatment.

options.text: Go to your car and leave because you don't want to be involved.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Leaving the scene of a major casualty incident delays crucial eyewitness info.

options.text: Start taking videos for social media.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You should be assisting with scene safety and communicating with 911.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! There was an earthquake at {location} and part of the kitchen wall collapsed! My dad is trapped under the fridge and I smell gas!

options.text: Evacuate the house immediately! A gas leak after an earthquake can cause a massive explosion.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A structural collapse combined with a gas leak is an imminent life threat.

options.text: Leave the doors open as you exit to vent the gas. Do not turn any switches on or off!
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Flipping a light switch creates a tiny spark that detonates the gas.

options.text: Stay in the kitchen to try to lift the fridge yourself.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You cannot lift a fridge alone, and you will die in the imminent gas explosion.

options.text: Light a match so you can see better in the dark.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Lighting a match in a gas leak instantly triggers a massive explosion.

options.text: Try to turn off the gas stove knobs.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The leak is likely in the broken wall pipe, not the stove knobs. Leave immediately.

options.text: Use your cell phone flashlight right next to the broken pipe to inspect it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Electronic devices can spark. Do not use them near the source of the leak.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I got out to the street! But my dad is still in there!

options.text: BFP is arriving with heavy rescue gear. Tell them exactly where he is.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Firefighters have explosive gas meters and the tools to lift heavy appliances safely.

options.text: Stay clear of the house in case there is an aftershock or an explosion.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Aftershocks can bring the rest of the unstable house down.

options.text: Run back in quickly to try one more time.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The gas has had more time to build up. Re-entering is suicide.

options.text: Go to the side of the house and break the kitchen window.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Breaking windows can cause sparks or shift the structure, triggering a collapse.

options.text: Try to locate the gas meter with a lighter.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A lighter will ignite any leaking gas outside as well.

options.text: Tell firefighters to ignore the gas and just run in.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Firefighters must secure the explosive hazard first or they will be killed along with your dad.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! We are having a BBQ at {location} and the propane tank is hissing really loudly and smells strongly of gas!

options.text: Get everyone away from the grill immediately. Do not try to turn it off if it's hissing.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A loud hiss indicates a major leak. Approaching it risks being caught in an explosion.

options.text: Evacuate the backyard. Do not light any cigarettes or use electronic devices near it.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Propane is highly explosive. Even a tiny spark from a phone can ignite it.

options.text: Go up and try to tighten the valve with a metal wrench.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Metal on metal can cause a spark, instantly detonating the gas cloud.

options.text: Throw water on it to stop the hissing.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water does nothing to stop a pressurized gas leak.

options.text: Light a long match to burn off the leaking gas safely.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This will cause an immediate and lethal explosion.

options.text: Try to unplug the grill if it's electric.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Unplugging cords creates a spark. Do not touch any electronics in a gas cloud.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We ran to the front of the house! The hissing is still so loud.

options.text: Stay out front and make sure no one walks down the side of the house.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Keeping a wide perimeter ensures safety if the tank detonates.

options.text: BFP will be there shortly with gas meters to secure the area.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Firefighters are equipped to shut off the gas safely.

options.text: Go to the backyard fence to peek over and see what it's doing.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: If it explodes, you are still too close.

options.text: Go back inside the house to watch from the kitchen window.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Gas can seep into the house. If it ignites, the house will catch fire.

options.text: Try to drive your car out of the driveway.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Starting a car engine creates sparks that could ignite the gas.

options.text: Tell your neighbor to jump the fence to look at it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You are putting your neighbor's life in danger.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! My daughter was playing with a sparkler at {location} and a spark caught her shirt on fire!

options.text: Tell her to STOP, DROP, and ROLL immediately! Cover her face with her hands.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: This is the most effective way to extinguish a clothing fire and protect the airway.

options.text: Grab a heavy blanket or towel to smother the flames on her.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Smothering cuts off oxygen to the fire quickly.

options.text: Tell her to run to the hose in the backyard.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Running feeds the fire with oxygen, making it burn hotter and faster.

options.text: Try to pat the fire out with your bare hands.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will severely burn your hands and it is too slow to stop the fire.

options.text: Try to pull the burning shirt over her head.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This drags the fire across her face and airway, causing lethal burns.

options.text: Tell her to jump up and down to shake the fire off.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Movement fans the flames.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: She rolled on the ground and it's out! But her arm is badly burned and her shirt is melted to it!

options.text: Run cool (not cold) water over the burn gently until BFP and medics arrive.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Cool water stops the burning process in the deep skin tissues.

options.text: Do not try to peel the melted shirt off her arm. Leave it alone.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Peeling melted fabric will tear the skin off with it. Medics must do it.

options.text: Put ice directly on the burn to numb the pain.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Ice restricts blood flow and causes frostbite to already damaged skin.

options.text: Smear butter or toothpaste over the burn.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Grease traps heat inside the burn and causes massive infections.

options.text: Rip the rest of the shirt off to get a better look.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will cause horrific tissue damage.

options.text: Wrap the burn tightly with a dry paper towel.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Paper towels stick to the burn and are painful to remove.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! I was removing my nail polish at {location} and the bottle spilled near a candle. The whole desk is on fire!

options.label: safe

transcript.text: I ran out and closed the door. I can hear the wood cracking inside!

options.label: unsafe

options.text: Run back to your bedroom to grab your purse.

options.text: Open the front door slightly to look down the hall.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Call your landlord before evacuating.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Life safety is the priority. Call the landlord from outside.

transcript.text: BFP! I left my laptop running on my bed at {location} and it overheated. The blanket is smoking and caught fire!

options.label: unsafe

options.text: Hide in the living room until the fire department gets here.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Open the front door to see if it makes the alarm stop.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Run back in to close the laptop lid.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Hit your car alarm button to scare him off.

options.text: Go outside and block the driveway so he can't leave.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: MDRRMO! My friend ran into a glass door at {location} and his arm is cut deep! Blood is spurting out in pulses!

options.text: Apply intense, direct pressure to the wound with a clean towel immediately! Do not let go!
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Spurting blood means an artery is cut. Heavy, constant pressure is the only way to save a life.

options.text: If the blood soaks through, do not remove the towel—put another one directly on top and press harder!
options.label: safe

options.text: Have him run his arm under cold tap water to clean it.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Try to pick the glass shards out first.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Glass acts as a plug. Removing it can unseal the artery and cause massive blood loss.

options.text: Wrap it lightly with a bandage.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Tell him to walk to the bathroom.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Walking increases heart rate and blood loss. Keep him seated or lying down.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I am pushing down as hard as I can! He says he feels lightheaded and cold!

options.label: safe
options.explanation: Lightheadedness and cold mean he is going into hypovolemic shock from blood loss.

options.text: Keep all your weight on that towel. The ambulance is turning onto your street.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Consistent pressure is critical. Medics will take over soon.

options.text: Let go of his arm to go open the front door.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: If you let go of an arterial bleed, he will lose a lethal amount of blood in seconds.

options.text: Give him a hot cup of tea to warm him up.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Sit him up so he doesn't pass out.

options.text: Slap his face to keep him awake.
options.label: unsafe

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: MDRRMO! My dad was fixing an outlet at {location} and got shocked! He is lying on the floor not moving!

options.explanation: If he is still touching the wire, touching him will electrocute you too.

options.text: Stay away from his body until you are 100% sure the electricity is cut off.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Rescuers becoming victims is the most common danger in electrical emergencies.

options.text: Grab his hand to pull him away from the outlet.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Human bodies conduct electricity. You will be shocked instantly.

options.text: Pour water on his face to wake him up.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water conducts electricity perfectly. This is lethal.

options.text: Push him with a metal broom handle.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Metal conducts electricity. Use only dry wood or rubber if absolutely forced to.

options.label: unsafe

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I flipped the main breaker off! The house is dark. He is still unresponsive.

options.text: Check if his chest is rising and falling. If he is not breathing, start CPR compressions.

options.text: Place your hands in the center of his chest and push hard and fast.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Correct instruction for bystander hands-only CPR.

options.label: unsafe

options.text: Try to force him to sit up in a chair.
options.label: unsafe

options.text: Put a pillow under his head to make him comfortable.
options.label: unsafe

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! A tanker truck crashed on the highway near {location} and green liquid is pouring out! People outside are coughing!

options.text: Stay in your car, roll up the windows, and turn off your air conditioning!

options.text: If you are outside, run upwind immediately. Chemical fumes are deadly.

options.text: Walk over to see if the truck driver needs help.

options.text: Drive through the puddle to escape.

options.text: Turn your car's AC on max to blow the smell away.
options.label: unsafe

transcript.speaker: Caller

transcript.text: Help! I'm hiding in the bathroom at the bank at {location}! Men with guns came in and someone was shot!

options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Throwing water on a live heating pad causes a massive electric shock.

options.text: Try to smother the fire with another blanket.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The fire will easily burn through the second blanket.

options.text: Tell her to roll out of bed quickly.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: An elderly person might fall and injure themselves. You must assist them.

options.text: Try to carry the burning mattress outside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Mattresses are heavy and you will drop fire throughout the house.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I got her out and closed the bedroom door. She is coughing a little.

options.text: Get completely out of the house. The smoke will spread.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A closed door buys time, but smoke will eventually seep out.

options.text: Wait outside. BFP and an ambulance are on the way to check her breathing.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Elderly lungs are very sensitive to toxic smoke inhalation.

options.text: Go to the kitchen and get her a glass of water.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Do not delay evacuation to get water.

options.text: Have her sit on the couch in the living room.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The living room will soon fill with deadly smoke.

options.text: Run back in for her medication.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Medication can be replaced. A life cannot.

options.text: Open the front windows to clear the smoke.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening windows creates a draft that feeds the bedroom fire.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! A car drove off with the gas nozzle still attached at {location} and the pump was ripped off and caught fire!

options.text: Hit the Emergency Shut-Off button if it is far away from the flames!
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Hitting the emergency stop cuts the underground fuel flow to the pumps instantly.

options.text: Evacuate the gas station immediately. Run far away from the underground tanks!
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Gas stations contain thousands of gallons of explosive fuel.

options.text: Try to put it out with a small fire extinguisher from your car.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A civilian extinguisher is useless against a pressurized fuel pump fire.

options.text: Drive your car closer to see what happened.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You are driving into a massive explosion hazard.

options.text: Run up to the pump to try to turn off the valve.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will be engulfed in flames.

options.text: Keep pumping gas at your pump since it's on the other side.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The entire station is at risk of a catastrophic explosion.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Someone hit the emergency shut-off! The fire on the pump is still burning but not spraying!

options.text: Keep everyone across the street. The residual fuel is still extremely dangerous.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Even with the flow stopped, the fire can still ignite vapors.

options.text: Ensure no one is smoking anywhere near the gas station.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Vapors travel far along the ground and can ignite easily.

options.text: Run into the convenience store to buy a drink.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The convenience store is in the blast radius.

options.text: Go to your car to get a closer video for social media.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Staying near the scene puts your life in danger.

options.text: Try to throw dirt on the burning pump.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Approaching the pump exposes you to toxic smoke and potential flare-ups.

options.text: Tell the cashier to stay inside and protect the register.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Property is not worth dying for. The cashier must evacuate.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! My toaster oven at {location} is completely on fire inside! There are flames shooting out the top!

options.text: Unplug the toaster oven if you can reach the cord safely, and do not open it.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Cutting the power removes the electrical hazard.

options.text: Keep the door of the toaster oven closed. Starving it of oxygen helps contain it.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Most small oven fires will burn themselves out if kept closed.

options.text: Open the toaster door to pull the burning food out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening it feeds oxygen to the fire and creates a massive flare-up in your face.

options.text: Throw a cup of water on it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water on a plugged-in appliance causes electrocution.

options.text: Try to pick the toaster oven up to throw it outside.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The metal casing is superheated. You will drop it and spread the fire.

options.text: Turn the toaster oven temperature up to burn it out faster.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Increasing heat makes the fire spread out of the appliance and onto the cabinets.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I unplugged it, but the flames reached the wooden cabinets above it!

options.text: Evacuate the house immediately. Kitchen cabinet fires spread into the walls and ceiling rapidly.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Once a fire reaches the structure, it is out of control for a civilian.

options.text: Get everyone outside and wait for BFP.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Life safety is the priority.

options.text: Try to hit the cabinets with a wet towel.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A wet towel cannot extinguish a structural wood fire.

options.text: Open the kitchen window to let the smoke out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Opening the window creates a draft that feeds the fire.

options.text: Hide in the living room and see if it stops.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The house will fill with toxic smoke in seconds.

options.text: Go to the bathroom to get the shower hose.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This wastes time and a small hose won't stop a cabinet fire.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: BFP! Someone threw a cigarette into my roof gutters at {location} and the dry leaves inside are burning!

options.text: Evacuate the house. A gutter fire can quickly ignite the roof structure and attic.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Roof fires are deadly because they burn above you, compromising the structure before you realize it.

options.text: Do not try to climb onto the roof to put it out. BFP is on the way.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Civilian ladder falls are common, and fighting fire at a height is extremely dangerous.

options.text: Climb a ladder with a bucket of water.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You cannot safely hold a ladder, climb, and carry a bucket while fighting a fire.

options.text: Go into the attic to check for flames.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The attic can fill with toxic smoke in seconds, trapping you inside.

options.text: Shoot fireworks at the gutter to knock the burning leaves out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This will just start more fires.

options.text: Ignore it, gutters are made of metal.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The heat from burning leaves will ignite the wooden eaves attached to the gutter.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We are outside. The flames are crawling under the roof shingles now!

options.text: Stay far back from the house. Ensure everyone in the family is accounted for.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A fully involved roof can collapse outwards.

options.text: Tell arriving firefighters exactly where you first saw the fire.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Knowing the origin helps BFP track the fire's path through the attic.

options.text: Run back in to save your computer.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never re-enter a building with a roof fire. It can collapse at any moment.

options.text: Try to spray the roof with a small garden hose.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: A garden hose cannot reach under shingles or into the attic where the fire is.

options.text: Move your car right up against the house to protect it from falling debris.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Your car will catch fire from radiant heat or falling burning shingles.

options.text: Break the windows so firefighters can get in faster.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Breaking windows unnecessarily feeds the fire with massive amounts of oxygen.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: PNP! A driver in a black truck is following me aggressively near {location}! He keeps honking and trying to run me off the road!

options.text: Keep driving and do NOT go home. Drive to the nearest police station or a crowded, well-lit area.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Going home shows the aggressor where you live. Public places deter violence.

options.text: Lock your doors and keep your windows rolled up. Do not stop your car.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Your moving vehicle is your best armor against an attacker.

options.text: Pull over to the side of the road to talk to him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Road rage attackers are often violently out of control. Do not confront them.

options.text: Slam on your brakes to scare him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Brake-checking will cause a high-speed collision and escalate the violence.

options.text: Drive to your house quickly and lock the door.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will lead a dangerous person to your family.

options.text: Throw a drink at his car out your window.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This is assault and will enrage him further.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: He just hit my bumper! We are still moving but I'm terrified!

options.text: I am sending PNP cruisers to your exact location now. Keep driving straight and stay on the line.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Live tracking is essential. Police will intercept the moving vehicles.

options.text: Turn your hazard lights on so officers can identify your car easily.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Visual markers help police spot you quickly in traffic.

options.text: Stop the car right there in the middle of the road.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Stopping makes you a sitting duck for assault or another collision.

options.text: Try to ram his truck back.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Vehicular combat is illegal and extremely deadly.

options.text: Speed up to 100 mph to lose him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: High-speed chases cause fatal accidents.

options.text: Drive the wrong way down a one-way street to trick him.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will hit an innocent driver head-on.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: MDRRMO! A tricycle just flipped over on the national highway at {location}! The passenger was thrown out and hit their head hard on the pavement!

options.text: Do not move the passenger! Keep them completely still and wait for the ambulance.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Moving someone with a potential spinal or severe head injury can cause permanent paralysis or death.

options.text: Tell arriving cars to slow down and direct traffic safely around the accident.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Securing the scene prevents secondary accidents from running over the victim.

options.text: Pick them up and try to carry them to the side of the road.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Unless the victim is in a burning vehicle, dragging them causes catastrophic spinal damage.

options.text: Take off their helmet if they are wearing one.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Removing a helmet without proper medical training can snap a broken neck.

options.text: Try to sit them up to give them water.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Sitting them up drops blood pressure to the brain, and water is a choking hazard.

options.text: Shake them by the shoulders to try to wake them up.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Violent shaking worsens traumatic brain injuries and neck fractures.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I am standing next to them directing traffic away. They are breathing but totally unconscious.

options.text: Kneel beside them and monitor their breathing continuously until MDRRMO arrives.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: If they stop breathing, you will need to start chest compressions immediately.

options.text: If they start to vomit, roll their entire body to the side at the same time to keep the airway clear.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: This is called a log-roll. It keeps the spine straight while preventing them from choking on vomit.

options.text: Turn their head to the side so they are more comfortable.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Twisting the neck alone can sever the spinal cord.

options.text: Try to force their eyes open to check their pupils.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Leave medical diagnostics to the professionals. You could damage their eyes.

options.text: Slap their cheeks gently to bring them back to consciousness.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Physical stimulus won't wake up a severe concussion and only causes harm.

options.text: Leave them there and try to flip the tricycle back over.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The patient is your priority. Flipping the trike could spill gasoline or cause a fire.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: MDRRMO! A snake just bit my leg while hiking near {location}! It hurts really badly and is swelling fast!

options.text: Sit down and stay completely still. Moving will pump the venom through your body faster.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Venom travels through the lymphatic system, which is driven by muscle movement.

options.text: Keep the bitten leg below the level of your heart to slow the venom spread.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Keeping it below the heart slows the venom's path to vital organs.

options.text: Try to suck the venom out with your mouth.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This is a myth. It does not remove venom and introduces dangerous mouth bacteria into the wound.

options.text: Tie a tight tourniquet around your leg to stop the venom.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Tourniquets concentrate the venom in one area, guaranteeing you will lose the limb to necrosis.

options.text: Run as fast as you can to the road.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Running will pump the venom straight to your heart and brain in minutes.

options.text: Cut an X over the bite mark to bleed the venom out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This causes severe bleeding, tissue damage, and terrible infections.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I am sitting still. I took a picture of the snake before it slithered away.

options.text: That is perfect! Show the picture to the paramedics so the hospital can prepare the right antivenom.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Identifying the snake ensures the correct and fastest medical treatment.

options.text: Remove any tight clothing, socks, or jewelry near the bite before the swelling gets worse.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Swelling from venom is massive. Rings or tight clothing will cut off circulation.

options.text: Go chase the snake to catch it for the hospital.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will get bitten again, and catching the snake delays your treatment.

options.text: Put ice directly on the bite to stop the swelling.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Ice on snake bites causes massive tissue damage and accelerates necrosis.

options.text: Drink a lot of alcohol to dull the pain.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Alcohol dilates blood vessels, spreading the venom faster.

options.text: Elevate your leg high above your head to stop the bleeding.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Elevating above the heart allows gravity to pull the venom straight to your vital organs.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! A massive tree just fell on a moving school bus at {location}! The roof is crushed and kids are trapped inside!

options.text: Do not try to move the heavy tree branches yourself. You could cause the roof to collapse further!
options.label: safe
options.explanation: The tree's weight is unstable. Moving it without heavy machinery can crush the victims.

options.text: Keep everyone calm and tell the kids inside to stay in their seats if they can't easily exit.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Panic inside a crushed vehicle causes secondary injuries. Waiting for rescue is safer.

options.text: Try to crawl through the broken windows to pull kids out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Crawling through jagged glass in an unstable structure will injure you and block rescue access.

options.text: Start cutting the tree with a chainsaw.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The vibrations and sudden weight shifts will cause the bus roof to collapse completely.

options.text: Tell the kids to push up on the roof to lift it.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Human strength cannot lift a multi-ton tree. Pushing it may destabilize it.

options.text: Drive your car into the tree to push it off.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Ramming the tree transfers lethal force directly to the children trapped beneath it.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Some kids climbed out the back emergency door. They are bleeding and crying!

options.text: Move the kids who escaped far away from the bus and the tree.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Getting survivors away from the hazard zone protects them from further collapse.

options.text: Have bystanders apply pressure to any bleeding wounds while MDRRMO arrives.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Basic first aid saves lives before professionals take over the triage.

options.text: Tell the escaped kids to go back in to help their friends.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Never send children into an unstable collapse zone.

options.text: Yell at the bus driver for crashing.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Blame is irrelevant during a rescue and causes unnecessary distress.

options.text: Try to carry the injured kids to your car to drive them to the hospital.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Moving trauma victims without stabilization causes spinal damage. Wait for ambulances.

options.text: Tell everyone to gather directly around the bus.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Crowds hinder emergency response and put more people in the danger zone.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Help! A small airplane just crashed into a house at {location}! The house is on fire and aviation fuel is everywhere!

options.text: Run far away from the crash site immediately! Aviation fuel is highly explosive!
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A plane crash is a massive hazmat and explosive incident. Distance is your only protection.

options.text: Do not go into the house or near the plane. BFP, PNP, and MDRRMO are responding in full force.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Civilians cannot survive or assist in an aviation fire. Professional firefighting foam is required.

options.text: Run up to the plane to pull the pilot out.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You will be caught in an inescapable fireball when the fuel ignites.

options.text: Try to spray the jet fuel with a garden hose.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Water spreads burning aviation fuel across the entire neighborhood, worsening the disaster.

options.text: Go into the burning house to look for survivors.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: The structural damage and jet fuel fire make the house an immediate death trap.

options.text: Pick up pieces of the plane from your yard as souvenirs.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Plane wreckage is toxic, sharp, and crucial federal evidence.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: I am standing down the street! The heat is incredible and there are smaller explosions happening!

options.text: Move even further back. Warn your neighbors to evacuate their houses immediately.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: Jet fuel fires spread incredibly fast through residential areas via radiant heat.

options.text: Keep the street completely clear for the incoming fire trucks and ambulances.
options.label: safe
options.explanation: A massive multi-agency response requires a lot of space to deploy safely.

options.text: Go closer to take a video for the news.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You are risking your life for a video. Stay away.

options.text: Try to direct traffic around the burning plane.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: You are staying too close to the explosion hazard. Let the police handle traffic.

options.text: Tell your neighbors to stay inside their houses.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: Nearby houses are at risk of catching fire. Evacuation is necessary.

options.text: Throw rocks at the wreckage to see if anyone moves.
options.label: unsafe
options.explanation: This is disrespectful, useless, and dangerous.
